The ring pipeline step by step, and the full 15-bird pilot level

All images embedded. Model: gemini-3.1-flash-image (~$0.01/call measured). This pilot ran calls sequentially; the editor fold-in rides the existing async job worker.

Step 1 — Background generation · 1 call · ~$0.01 · ~9s

One text-to-image call from the editor's assembled recipe prompt. Output 1024x1024. Actual prompt excerpt:

[Purpose]
Create a full-bleed portrait mobile-game background for Find the Bird.

[Short Description]
A pirate treasure-cove camp sprawling across a sheltered beach arranged as an organic isometric hidden-object scene.

[Scene] A pirate treasure-cove camp sprawling across a sheltered beach — a main campfire clearing ringed with driftwood seats, a side path branching up to a lookout ledge, a strip of tide-line rocks trailing off along the water. The entire ground surface is consistent sand and weathered rock throughout — every area the viewer can see the ground, it reads as rippled beach sand, …

Step 2 — Upscale · 0 calls · $0

Deterministic Lanczos 4x to 4096 (deterministic-lanczos-4x in session provenance — not ESRGAN). The whole image scales together, so relative line weight is preserved; no model touches pixels here.

Step 3 — Hitbox placement · 0 calls · $0

Geometry-safe placement on the clean background. The rings are simultaneously paint targets and tap targets, so hitbox alignment is by construction:

Step 4 — Ring paint-in · 1 call per bird · ~$0.01 · ~10s each

input: clean crop + magenta ring
output: bird painted in scene (bird 09, drift 6%)
recovered cutout = diff inside ring

Step 5 — Recovery + paste-back · 0 calls · $0

The playable scene = clean background + the feathered ring interior of each output. Painted-in pixels, deterministic delivery; drift outside the ring is discarded:

bird 03 input
raw output — drift 77%, whole crop re-rendered
what the level gets: ring interior only

Step 6 — Ship lane (established) · 0 calls · $0

Hitbox recenter -> sprite/mask/meta -> recomposite -> export -> webp -> manifest upsert.

Prompt provenance — what differs from prompts.py (deviation, flagged)

The editor's default magenta mode uses FILLED discs + a prompt composed from the session's dog_prompt (charm/variation/species-readability/realistic-scale clauses) via _magenta_prompt(). This pilot used a hand-written ring prompt that KEPT blending/ring-removal/ pixel-preservation but DROPPED the charm, cross-crop variation, and anti-magenta-bleed clauses — visible in the output: pilot birds are more generic/repetitive than A's characterful ones. The editor fold-in composes a _ring_prompt(dog_prompt) exactly like _magenta_prompt does, so the default charm/variation language comes back.

This is a crop of an illustrated hidden-object scene. A magenta circle outline marks a target spot. Paint exactly one small charming bird INSIDE the marked circle, fully blended into the scene [...] Then remove the magenta circle completely [...] every pixel outside the circle, and every pixel inside the circle that is not the bird or its shadow, must remain EXACTLY as in the input.
